Harvesting rounds only 15.32 vs 24 in 2025 (PA); harvesters 17 vs 21 needed and 29 workers vs 35 (Mar 2026).
Pruning behind in PM05E (22% in Q1) and 2026 manuring 24% by March; hilly PM15G3 rehabilitation and road upgrade still pending.
PA and Agro disagree on Dec 2025 rat damage (under 10% vs 10–13%); no baiting in Q1 2026.

issues.title: Dec 2025 rat damage: under 10% (PA) vs over 10% (Agro)
issues.detail: PA Table 16 shows 8.0–10.0% per block (average 8.94%, below threshold). Agro Table 17 shows 10.0–13.0% in every block for Dec 2025 and 8.0–10.0% for Jan 2026. The PA calls it under control while Agro says baiting was incomplete and must continue until bait acceptance is below 20%.

issues.title: Cost per tonne: RM193.10 vs RM191.10
issues.detail: PA Table 28 and 9.1 give RM193.10 (items add to 193.09) but concluding remarks 13.11 and the reply table say RM191.10. Budget RM230.86 is described as per hectare; it is per tonne.

issues.title: Ganoderma figures and advice differ
issues.detail: PA Table 17: 129 of 13,736 palms shown as 0.009%; it is about 0.94%. E2 is listed as 46 ha vs 26 ha in the blocking system. PA says no census is needed; Agro 4.5.7 advises a census and de-boling.

issues.title: Soil/water conservation overspend unexplained
issues.detail: PA Table 6: RM29,376 vs RM3,168 budget (RM60.82 vs 6.56 per ha). The text does not explain it.

issues.title: Harvesting intervals and counts differ
issues.detail: PA says intervals under 15 days in Mar 2026; Agro Table 12 gives Jan 2026 intervals of 14–22 days (PM15G 20–22), yet Agro 6.9 says two rounds a month were maintained. Harvesters are 17 in PA Table 3 but 20 in the text (including drivers/loaders).

issues.title: Block hectares swapped in rat baiting tables
issues.detail: PA Tables 14–15 and Agro Table 18 list F1–F4 as 22/39/66/19 ha and G1–G4 as 33/45/56/30 ha; the blocking system has F1–F4 33/45/56/30 and G1–G4 22/39/66/19.

issues.title: OER far below budget, not discussed
issues.detail: PA Table 26: OER 13.94% vs 19.00% budget (17.08% in 2024); CPO 3.25 vs 4.48 t/ha. Neither report comments.

issues.title: Road grading and Q1 crop figures inconsistent
issues.detail: Road grading is 748.57 chains in the table and reply but 784.57 in 6.4.1 (66% of 1,190). PA 8.3 gives the to-date budget as 2,577 t and also quotes 3.47 t/ha for it, while Table 27 estimate is 2,572 t and 5.33 t/ha.

issues.title: Fertiliser programme items missing in Agro appendix
issues.detail: PA Table 13 and Agro Table 9 list Mix A 31.8 mt and NK1 31.8 mt for 2026, but Agro Appendix 1 has no Mix A or NK1 for Insan Jaya fields, and no entry for PM03C1.

issues.title: Rainfall totals do not add up
issues.detail: Agro Appendix 2: 2024 stated 2,093 mm / 116 days but months add to 2,429 mm / 131 days; 2025 stated 140 days but months add to 155 (mm 2,739 agrees). Dashboard leaves 2024 blank and 2025 days blank.

actions.item: Recruit 4 more harvesters and consider mechanised infield collection (EV Badang)
Bring pruning up to date, especially PM05E (22% in Q1) and PM03C1
Finish 2026 manuring on schedule; use pre-measured containers
Review manuring piece rate (RM64.40/day) and PM05E harvester pay (RM63.00/day), both below RM65.38 minimum wage
Rat control per SOP: quarterly census, baiting until acceptance under 20%
Rehabilitate PM15G3: access paths, pruning, clear bracken, bamboo and jungle trees
Upgrade hilly roads in PM15G2 and G3; start 2026 road grading
Eradicate VOPs, Stenochlaena, wild bamboo and epiphytes
Rake palm circles to remove oxidised loose fruit; stop leaving rejected unripe bunches in the field
Monitor magnesium deficiency in hilly PM14F3
Use GIS census palm density for fertiliser and fieldwork
Do selective weeding before circle spraying; consider CDA
Keep harvesting intervals at 15 days or less in all fields

LADANG INSAN JAYA, Insan Jaya Sendirian Berhad (Prosper group). Fact pack drawn from PA Report 1/2026 (Planting Advisor En. Adnan Bin Mustafa, visit 8 April 2026, reviewing Jan-Dec 2025 and Jan-Mar 2026) and Agronomy Report 1/2026 for Ladang Darabif and Insan Jaya (Agronomists En. Alison Bin Janari, Junior Agronomist, and Mr Chong Kuan Ming, Senior Agronomist; visit 10 February 2026; previous Agro visit 22 September 2025). General Manager Mr. Lee Chong Yew. Estate Manager Mr. Asuraja S/O Krishnan (joined March 2026; also manages Darabif). Assistant Manager in charge En. Mohd Bukhari Bin Wahab was to transfer to Darabif on 18 April 2026 with no replacement, leaving the estate directly under the Darabif manager. The previous PA visit was 18 December 2025 by Mr Boey Chee Weng.

AREA (PA Table 1, March 2026; Agro Tables 1 and 4): planted 483.00 ha, all mature, 136 palms per ha in the census: PM03C1 55 ha, PM05E 118 ha (E1 92, E2 26), PM14F 164 ha (F1 33, F2 45, F3 56, F4 30), PM15G 146 ha (G1 22, G2 39, G3 66, G4 19). Vacant plantable (ravine) 5.00 ha, unplantable hilly and rocky 30.00 ha, estate title 518.00 ha. Planting years from the contractor table: 2003 (C1), 2005 (E), 2014 (F), 2015 (G). Palm census by the PARAS GIS/drone team is complete: 65,688 palms, SPH 136 in every block (Agro Table 5); the PA says the data should now drive fertiliser and fieldwork. Agro said the drone census was still being finalised and not yet in the area statement. Age profile of both estates 11 to 23 years; replanting not required.

STAFF (PA): 1 Estate Manager, 2 Field Supervisors (Muhamad Faiezudin; Muhammad Zulfaizul joined March 2026) and 1 office clerk; judged adequate. A trainee field conductor resigned in December 2025.

LABOUR (PA Table 3, March 2026): total 29 workers vs 35 required (-6); 26 at the last visit and 23 the month before. Harvesters 17 vs 21 required (-4), driver/loaders 3 vs 5 (-2), weeding 2 vs 2, manuring 5 vs 5, other 2 vs 2. Including drivers and loaders the PA counts 20 harvesting workers, ratio 1 to 24 ha against 1 to 20 ha recommended; 4 more are needed because there is no mechanised infield collection. Worker ratio 1 to 17 ha (optimum 1 to 14). A single contractor, Lee Kok Yong, carries all work with 29 workers against 32 required (Table 4). The Group MD earlier asked that harvesting and manuring workers be deployed from Darabif as needed.

GENERAL CHARGES (PA Table 5, 2025): actual RM432,427.64 vs budget RM684,925 (37% below); RM895.30 per ha vs RM1,418.06. Management and supervision RM294,003.08 (RM608.70/ha vs 796.57); labour and amenities RM83,606.43 (RM173.10 vs 197.04); other RM54,818.13 (RM113.50 vs 424.45; quit rent and cess nil vs RM109,828 budget; security RM3,632 vs RM33,622). Over budget: labour recruitment +RM7,354 (24%), interest +RM640 (21%). Including depreciation RM40,948.19 total general charges RM473,375.83. Capital expenditure: budget RM4,000 (staff quarters furniture), nothing spent.

UPKEEP AND CULTIVATION (PA Table 6, 2025): total RM943,757.63 vs RM1,148,033.07 budget; RM1,953.95 per mature ha vs RM2,376.90. Per ha actual vs budget: weeding 187.07 vs 222.67 (selective 110.23 vs 115.79; circle 76.84 vs 106.88); manuring 1,369.57 vs 1,765.16 (labour 86.24 vs 168.62, material 1,283.33 vs 1,596.54); pest and disease 56.77 vs 63.32 (rat baiting 56.02 vs 52.54); census nil vs 5.66; drains nil vs 18.67; roads and bridges 202.66 vs 206.75; soil and water conservation 60.82 vs 6.56 (RM29,376 vs RM3,168, no explanation given); boundaries 1.83 vs 3.28; pruning 75.23 vs 84.83.

WEEDING (PA): Circle spraying 2025: 1,276 of 1,449 ha, 2.6 of 3 rounds (88%); PM03C1 and PM05E 2.0 rounds, PM14F and PM15G 3.0. Selective 2025: 1,139 of 1,449 ha, 2.4 rounds (79%); PM14F and PM15G 2.0 rounds, others 3.0. Q1 2026: selective 1.0 round on all 483 ha; circle 173 ha (0.3 round, 12%) completing last year's PM03C1 and PM05E programme. Sprayer output 5.0 to 6.0 ha per man-day at RM15 per ha, earning RM75 to RM90 per day. Circle spray: CKS low-volume nozzle 200 L per ha with 150 mL glyphosate per 18 L; selective: mist blower about 50 L per ha with 250 mL triclopyr (Ranger) and 30 g metsulfuron methyl. PA suggests CDA with glyphosate, selective before circle, and using one circle round to kill VOPs and Stenochlaena with sodium chlorate. Ageratum regenerating in PM14F1 and F2. Agro (Feb 2026): three interrow rounds in 2025 only complete in PM03C; circle complete only in PM14F and PM15G; manpower diverted to manuring. Giant paspalum in G2; Clidemia hirta patches in F1, F2, E1; woody scrub, Stenochlaena, bracken and wild bamboo in hilly G3 and G4; VOPs in F3 and G4 (recently rehabilitated areas); large epiphytes in E1 and E2 being poisoned; ground condition not entirely satisfactory in terraces.

MANURING (PA): 2025 programme 734.75 mt, delivered 716.75 mt, applied 624.95 mt (85.06%) at Dec 2025, delayed by late delivery. Cost RM1,369.57 per ha, 22% below budget. 2026 programme 689.49 mt: Mix B 518.19, Mix A 31.8, CIRP/ARP 74.1, kieserite 33.6, NK1 31.8. To March: 168.15 mt applied (24%): Mix B 132.45 mt (26%), kieserite 18.85 of 33.6 mt (56%), NK1 16.85 of 31.8 mt (53%), Mix A and CIRP nil. Manual broadcasting (wheelbarrow, bucket on terraces) at 28 bags per man-day for 2.0 kg per palm, RM2.30 per bag = RM64.40 per day, below the RM65.38 minimum wage; PA advises discussing a fair rate with senior management. Agro: 2025 programme completed in January 2026 (Mix B 581.4 mt, CIRP/ARP 109.65 mt, kieserite 43.7 mt, all 100%), but with delays of 2 to 4 months (Table 8). 2026 progress by early February: Mix B 13.75 of 518.19 mt (3%), others nil. In F3 Mix B 2.25 kg per palm by 3 workers, 105 bags, about 35 bags per person; quality acceptable with minimal lumps, narrow bands and caking; use pre-measured containers. 2026 programme (Agro Appendix 1, kg per palm): PM05E E1 and E2 Mix B 9.0 sub-soil (Jan) plus kieserite 0.75; PM14F F1-F4 Mix B 2.25 in four rounds plus kieserite 0.75 and rock phosphate 1.75; PM15G G1 and G2 Mix B 2.25 (Feb), kieserite 1.00, Mix B 2.00, Mix B 2.25, rock phosphate 1.50, Mix B 2.00; G3 and G4 Mix B 9.0 sub-soil (Jan), kieserite 0.75, rock phosphate 2.00. PM03C1 has no entry in the Insan Jaya appendix extract. Specs: Mix B 45% SOA, 40% MOP, 14% kieserite, 1% borate; rock phosphate 28-30% P2O5; kieserite 27% MgO.

PEST AND DISEASE: Rat baiting: two campaigns of three rounds each over 310 ha in 2025 (PA Tables 14, 15), bait acceptance in round 3 of campaign 2 still 14% to 47%. Agro: campaign incomplete, only a few blocks below 20% acceptance; do not stop until acceptance is consistently under 20%; standard procedure is quarterly census, one baiting round (one bait per palm) in blocks over threshold, follow-up census a month later. Rat damage census: PA Dec 2025 8.0 to 10.0% per block (average 8.94%, below 10% threshold); Agro Dec 2025 10.0 to 13.0% per block (all above threshold) and Jan 2026 8.0 to 10.0% (F1 9.0, F2 9.5, F3 8.5, F4 8.5, G1 8.0, G2 9.0, G3 10.0, G4 9.5). No baiting done Jan-Mar 2026 (PA). Fresh rat attack seen at a platform. Bagworm: none seen. Ganoderma: PA Table 17 (Dec 2025) 129 affected of 13,736 palms in PM03C1 and PM05E2 (shown as 0.009%; 129 of 13,736 is about 0.94%), PA says no census necessary; Agro says Ganoderma is sporadic and advises a census and de-boling. Magnesium deficiency symptoms in hilly F3. Palm vigour improved in hilly G3 and G4 but deficiency symptoms persist.

ROADS AND DRAINS (PA): Road grading 748.57 chains (text also quotes 784.57) of 1,190 chains budget at RM10 per chain; lateriting 196.03 of 200 chains at RM95; backhoe 856 hours (RM45); excavator 288 hours (RM90); roadside frond pruning 966 ha at RM2.50 per ha. Roads passable but hilly roads in PM15G2 and G3 need upgrading with motor grader, backhoe, laterite and crusher run; grading needed in PM14F1. 2026 road work not yet started. No drain desilting in 2025 (300 chains budget), no expenditure; drains flowing freely.

REHABILITATION AREA PM15G3 (PA section 12): about 12 ha of hilly land; work since early 2025, about 5 ha still to complete at Dec 2025. Palms pruned and terrace paths sprayed, but bracken, jungle trees and bamboo between terraces are thick. Priorities: build access roads and paths, expedite pruning and removal of rotten bunches and oxidised loose fruit, then clear jungle trees, bamboo, VOPs and bracken systematically.

PRUNING (PA): 2025 progressive pruning 5,244 of 5,796 ha (90%); PM03C1, PM14F, PM15G 100%, PM05E 864 of 1,416 ha (61%). Q1 2026: 1,118 of 1,449 ha (77%): PM03C1 67%, PM05E 22%, PM14F and G 100%. Agro Jan 2026: PM05E only 26 of 118 ha (22%). Under-pruning with hanging dried fronds in PM05E1 and PM03C1; slight over-pruning in G4 corrective areas; frond stacking improved on flat land but not fully satisfactory.

HARVESTING (PA, Agro): 20 contractor workers, cutter-and-carrier with wheelbarrows; one mini tractor with highlift trailer serves PM14F and G; manual loading in PM03C and PM05E; FFB goes to Rompin Palm Oil Mill. EV Badang mechanised collection suggested. Harvester output March 2026 (Table 22): PM03C1 2.04 t per man-day at RM35 per t, RM71.40; PM05E 1.80 t at RM35, RM63.00 (below minimum wage); PM14F 4.10 t at RM40, RM164.00; PM15G 3.34 t at RM40, RM133.60. Rounds 2025 (target 24): PA average 15.32; C1 13, E 16, F 16.13, G 16.13 (Agro Table 28: 54% to 67% of target). Q1 2026 rounds: 5.50 (C1), 5.00 (E), 6.00 (F), 6.00 (G), average 5.63 against 6.0. PA says intervals under 15 days by March 2026. Agro monthly intervals 2025 mostly 18 to 28 days in F and G and 13 to 24 in C and E; Jan 2026 C 16-20, E 14-19, F 16-14 (as printed), G 20-22 days. Quality: platforms 100% to 95% ripe in G3; underripe bunches rejected by platform pre-check left in F3; unharvested bunches after corrective pruning in F3; oxidised loose fruit in circles near drains and boundary (rake circles). Harvesting cost 2025: RM795,820 = RM70.75 per t vs RM69.77 budget (contract 44.61, internal transport 15.43, external transport 10.72).

CROP (PA Table 26, 2025): FFB 11,248.14 t vs budget 11,381 t (99%); 2024 10,791.41 t. Yield 23.29 t/ha vs 23.56 budget and 22.34 in 2024. CPO 1,567.90 t, OER 13.94% vs 19.00% budget and 17.08% in 2024; CPO 3.25 t/ha vs 4.48 budget. Kernel 552.16 t (4.91%). Jan-Mar 2026 (Table 27): 1,673.82 t against estimate 2,572 t (65%), 3.47 t/ha vs estimate 5.33 t/ha; year estimate 12,244 t (25.35 t/ha). Fields: PM03C1 185.72 t (3.38 t/ha vs est 5.45), PM05E 362.90 t (3.08 vs 5.40), PM14F 606.83 t (3.70 vs 5.49), PM15G 518.37 t (3.55 vs 5.03). Agro yield 2025 (2024) t/ha: C1 23.32 (25.62), E 18.73 (23.02), F 28.47 (23.88), G 21.14 (18.84); estate 23.29 (22.34), +4.3%. Agro Jan 2026 (Jan 2025): C1 1.17 (1.37), E 1.47 (1.46), F 1.46 (1.39), G 1.69 (0.90); estate 1.50 (1.26), +19%, still below expectation; focus on hilly areas. Yield-limiting factors named by Agro: extended harvesting intervals, fertiliser deviations, pruning delays, extensive rat attack in P14 and P15.

PRODUCTION COST (PA Table 28, 2025): ex-estate RM193.10 per t FFB vs RM230.86 budget (16% lower): general charges 38.44 vs 60.18; upkeep and cultivation 83.90 vs 100.91; harvesting and collection 70.75 vs 69.77. PA text elsewhere quotes RM191.10.

VEHICLE (PA): one Toyota Hilux AKL 1918 (2016), RM2,147.42 monthly average, RM0.27 per km vs RM0.74 budget.

RAINFALL (Agro Appendix 2, group record): 2023 157 rain days, 2,965 mm. 2025 monthly mm add to 2,739 mm (stated), stated 140 days though monthly days add to 155. 2024 stated 2,093 mm and 116 days but monthly entries add to 2,429 mm and 131 days (stated totals appear to omit December). Jan 2026 5 days, 34 mm.

ADVICE AND OUTLOOK: PA: use GIS census density for fertiliser, add 4 harvesters, rehabilitate PM15G3, upgrade hilly roads, update pruning (PM05E, PM03C1), keep vigilant on rats and bagworm. Agro: finish 2026 manuring on schedule, keep intervals at 15 days or less, rat control per SOP, eradicate VOPs and bamboo, census and de-bole Ganoderma.

DATA CAVEATS: rat damage Dec 2025 differs between PA and Agro; cost per t 193.10 vs 191.10; Ganoderma percentage and E2 hectares; baiting table hectares for F and G blocks appear swapped; soil and water conservation overspend; harvester counts 17 vs 20. See issues.

notes: Harvest items are per-tonne as printed in Table 25 (they sum to 70.76 actual vs printed 70.75, rounding). Upkeep and general-charge items are calc: RM amounts in Tables 6 and 5 divided by FFB 11,248.14 actual / 11,381.00 budget (Table 28).

Upkeep budget items (Table 6) sum to RM1,148,033.07 vs RM1,148,478 in Table 28 (RM445 gap); group budget 100.91 is Table 28's. Actual upkeep items sum RM943,757.63 vs 943,758.00. General charges items sum exactly to Table 28.

Report text elsewhere (exec summary and section 13) quotes RM191.10/t for total production cost vs RM193.10 in Table 28 and 9.1; Table 28 figure used (matches dashboard 193.1). Budget quoted there as 'per hectare' is a typo.

Mix B round 1: planned Jan, done Feb to May (up to 4 months late; some 3 months); round 2: planned Apr, done May to Aug (up to 4 months); round 3: planned Jul, done Oct-Nov (3-4 months). Certain blocks 2-3 months late (blocks not named in the extract).

Jan 16.00 (Mix B); Apr 0.40 (borate); May 57.55; Jun 49.50 (1st half 123.45 t = 27.94% of 441.85 required); Jul 13.40; Aug 107.0 (97.70 Mix B + 9.25 RP, split uncertain); Sep 62.40; Oct 114.65 (76.20 Mix B, 26.90 KIE, 11.55 RP); Nov 127.75 (115.35 Mix B, 7.40 KIE, 5.00 RP); Dec 76.35 Mix B = 624.95 t. Mix B 518.19 t programme, 89.3 delivered, 13.75 applied (3%); Mix A 31.8, CIRP/ARP 74.1, KIE 33.6, NK1 31.8: none delivered or applied. Limited progress as the estate completed 2025 carry-over.

Mix B 518.19 t required, 132.45 applied (26%); Mix A 31.80, nil (0%); ARP/CIRP 74.10, nil (0%); KIE 33.60 required, 18.05 received, 18.85 applied as printed (56%); NK1 31.80 required, 14.95 received, 16.85 applied (53%, balance stock 14.95); total 689.49 t, 168.15 t applied = 24%. PA: progress acceptable.

Surface broadcast throughout, wheelbarrow, bucket on terraces. 28 bags/man-day at 2.0 kg dose, RM2.30/bag = RM64.40/day, below the minimum wage RM65.38/day; PA advises a fair rate. spraying.v: Weeding RM187.07/ha vs RM222.67 (84%): selective RM110.23/ha, circle RM76.84/ha. Circle CKS low-volume, 200 L/ha with 150 mL glyphosate in 18 L; selective 10 L mist blower 50 L/ha with 250 mL Triclopyr (Ranger) and 30 g Metsulfuron methyl (Canyon). Contractor RM36 (circle) / RM39 (selective) per ha, worker RM15/ha, 5.0-6.0 ha per man-day, RM75-90/day. PA/Group MD: low-volume Inter Pump or CDA with glyphosate would improve productivity; do selective first then circle.

2025: circle 1,276 ha of 1,449 ha = 2.6 rounds (88%); selective 1,139 ha = 2.4 rounds (79%). Mar 2026: circle 173 ha = 0.3 round (12%); selective 483 ha = 1 round (33%). One circle round may be used for VOP and Stenochlaena eradication (contact herbicide e.g. sodium chlorate, high-volume nozzle). Agro: weeding slower than expected; circle spraying overdue in all blocks in Jan 2026; four rounds completed in F and G circle only.

pests.v: Estate rat census Dec 2025 8.94% (143 of 1,600 palms, 8 blocks) PA; pest and disease cost RM56.77/ha (89% of RM63.31); two campaigns of 3 rounds across 310 ha, baiting RM56.02/ha (RM27,060). Bagworm: no signs (PA). No baiting as of Mar 2026; census every 3 months.

other.v: Estate title 518 ha: planted/mature 483.00 ha (C1 55, E 118, F 164, G 146); 5.00 ha plantable vacant (ravine) and 30.00 ha unplantable hilly/rocky vacant. Drone/GIS census complete (PA); area statement unchanged.

11,248.14 t FFB = 23.29 t/ha vs budget 11,381 t (23.56 t/ha) = 99%; 2024 10,791.41 t = 22.34 t/ha (+4.3%). CPO 1,567.90 t (13.94% vs 19.00% budget); kernel 552.16 t (4.91%). Jan-Mar 2026: 1,673.82 t = 3.47 t/ha, 65% of estimated 2,572 t (PA text 2,577 t; 5.33 t/ha). Jan 2026 yield 1.50 t/ha vs 1.26 in Jan 2025 (+19%), 'below expectation' (Agro). 2025 average harvest rounds 15.32 vs 24 required; average 2026 5.63 rounds in Q1.

Extended harvest intervals (harvester shortage), manuring deviations, delayed pruning, extensive rat attack particularly in P14 and P15. Estate not meeting 24 rounds a year (15.32 in 2025). Hilly areas need most attention.

29 workers vs 35 required (+3 on 26 at last visit; 23 the previous month): harvesters 17 vs 21, drivers/loaders 3 vs 5, weeding 2 vs 2, manuring 5 vs 5, other 2 vs 2. 20 harvesters incl. drivers/loaders = 1 per 24 ha (needs 4 more; target 1 per 20 ha), no infield mechanisation; EV Badang suggested. Estate Manager Mr Asuraja (joined Mar 2026, also manages Darabif); Assistant Manager in charge En Mohd Bukhari Wahab transferring to Darabif on 18 Apr 2026, no replacement; Field Supervisor En Muhammad Zulfaizul joined 16 Mar 2026; a Trainee Field Conductor resigned Dec 2025. Establishment: 1 manager, 2 field supervisors, 1 clerk, security guard.

Cost of production RM193.10/t FFB (table) vs RM230.86 budget, 16% lower (PA text RM191.10): general charges RM38.44/t, upkeep RM83.90, harvesting RM70.75. General charges RM895.30/ha (RM432,427.64) vs RM1,418.06, 37% below. Upkeep RM1,953.95/ha vs RM2,376.90. Harvest and collection RM70.75/t vs RM69.77 (+1.40%): contract RM44.61, internal transport RM15.43, external RM10.72. Overspent lines: labour recruitment RM7,354 (24%), interest RM640 (21%).

Weeding RM187.07/ha; manuring RM1,369.57; pests RM56.77; drains nil (budget RM18.67, 300 chains of 5x4x3 ft not desilted, drainage free-flowing); roads RM202.66 (98% of 206.75); soil/water conservation RM60.82 (budget 6.56); boundary RM1.83; pruning RM75.23 (84.83); census/thinning nil (budget 5.66).

Grading 748.57 chains of 1,190 budgeted (66%; PA text 784.57), RM10/chain; lateriting/gravelling 196.03 of 200 chains at RM95; backhoe 856 h at RM45; excavator 288 h at RM90; roadside frond pruning 966 ha, 2 rounds at RM2.50/ha. 2026 road work not started; complete grading in the first half. Estate borders government tarmac road and tapping-right area: watch for FFB theft.
2025: 140 rain days, 2,739 mm (2024: 116 days, 2,093 mm); Jan 2026 5 days, 34 mm. Heavy rain restricted hilly access in 2025.
Toyota Hilux AKL 1918, running RM0.27/km vs RM0.74 budget. Capital budget RM4,000 (new staff quarters furniture) not spent.

blockGaps: No rat census or baiting data for P03C1 or P05E (the census covers F and G only). No block-level leaf or soil analysis in either report. No weeding table text for 2025 beyond the garbled Agro Table 15 (round columns read by position, which conflicts with PA on whether P05E had 3 inter-row rounds: PA 3.0 rounds, Agro only P03C).
